response.rationale: Bilateral acute knee inflammation after Synvisc with high synovial WBCs and negative cultures is classic pseudoseptic arthritis; septic arthritis is excluded by negative cultures and lack of systemic signs, while aseptic reaction labels are less specific.

rejected.why: Negative gram stain/cultures and absence of fever, chills, or malaise make septic arthritis unlikely despite inflammatory synovial fluid.
No preceding infection is described; symptoms are temporally tied to intra-articular Synvisc injection rather than a remote reactive trigger.
Accurate as an aseptic post-injection arthritis but less specific than pseudoseptic arthritis for this inflammatory pattern.
Broad reaction label; pseudoseptic arthritis better captures the synovial fluid leukocytosis with negative cultures.
